project_goal: Real-time Digital Twin and Predictive Maintenance for AGV Fleet (5000 units)
architecture_style: Event-Driven Microservices with High-Performance Ingestion Layer

components.purpose: Decouple AGV telemetry from processing services. Provide reliable, low-latency communication for 5,000+ devices.

implementation_details.protocol: MQTT v5.0 (for improved session management and properties)
implementation_details.qos_level: QoS 1 (At Least Once) for critical telemetry
implementation_details.security: TLS/SSL (mTLS) for device authentication and data encryption in transit

components.role: Central processing unit for AGV data. Implements the Single Source of Truth (SSOT).

implementation_details.language: Go (for high concurrency and low latency processing)

data_ingestion.process: Receive message -> validate schema -> update Redis cache (hot state) -> buffer for batch writing to InfluxDB.

implementation_details.data_storage_hot: Redis (Key-Value Store) for immediate state retrieval. Key: agv:{agv_id}, Value: JSON-encoded Digital Twin snapshot.
implementation_details.data_storage_historical: InfluxDB (Time Series Database) for high-frequency writes and long-term analysis. Measurement: agv_telemetry.
implementation_details.security: JWT/OIDC validation for internal API endpoints, RBAC enforcement.

components.role: Predictive maintenance trigger based on time-series analysis.

implementation_details.process: Cron-based worker or stream processing logic. Queries InfluxDB data using Flux language window functions to detect specific patterns (e.g., vibration > 3.5 for 60 seconds AND temperature > 75C).
implementation_details.output: If anomaly detected, update AGV state in Redis to PREDICTIVE_MAINTENANCE and send an alert via internal messaging system or database flag.

components.role: Distribute hot state data to the mission control dashboard efficiently.

implementation_details.protocol: WebSockets (for full-duplex communication and minimal overhead)
implementation_details.data_format: Binary serialization (Protobuf) over WebSockets for performance optimization.
implementation_details.source: Listens for updates from Redis/Digital Twin Service and broadcasts updates to connected clients (Frontend).

components.role: Operator interface for real-time monitoring and command issuance.

implementation_details.visualization_engine: Canvas 2D/WebGL for high-performance rendering of 5,000 entities without DOM manipulation overhead.
implementation_details.data_source: WebSockets for real-time map updates; REST API for historical data queries and command issuance.
implementation_details.styling: TailwindCSS with high-contrast theme (dark mode) for industrial accessibility.

data_flow_summary: 2. Digital Twin Service (Go) consumes MQTT -> Validates -> Updates Redis (Hot State) -> Batches Writes to InfluxDB (Historical)
3. Heuristics Engine queries InfluxDB -> Detects anomaly -> Updates Redis status (PREDICTIVE_MAINTENANCE)
4. Streaming API (Go) reads Redis updates -> Pushes to Frontend via WebSockets
5. Frontend operator sends Command -> REST API endpoint -> Digital Twin Service -> Publishes Command to MQTT Broker (commands/agv/{id})
justification_database_choice: InfluxDB is chosen over relational databases like PostgreSQL because its schema-less nature and time-series-optimized storage engine allow for millions of write operations per second with high data compression. For 2.500 ops/s, a relational database would suffer from index bloat and significantly slower ingestion rates, violating the high-performance requirement. Redis serves as the low-latency cache for immediate access to the current state, preventing unnecessary queries to InfluxDB for every dashboard update.
